title: Privileged website deployment executes mutable action tags
trigger: A new main deployment or manual dispatch after an upstream v4 tag moves
impact: The same reviewed website revision can execute different third-party code with OIDC ability to assume the site deploy role. IAM grants object writes/deletes and CloudFront invalidation, so mutable action identity can bypass source review for a privileged deployment. No upstream compromise is alleged.
reproduction_status: static configuration and IAM trust-path inspection
remediation: Pin checkout and AWS credential action to reviewed immutable commit SHAs; update them by reviewed changes. Restrict id-token permission to the deploy job.
scope_note: Existing integration-snapshot weakness; not asserted newly introduced by ADL diff.

title: Builder reconstruction still resolves mutable and unverified executable inputs
trigger: Rebuild the canonical builder from the same committed Dockerfile at a later date
impact: Ubuntu tag, Rust stable/rustup and unchecked AWSCLI/sccache/llvm-cov downloads may change outside reviewed source identity. Resolving a built image digest protects consumption, not reconstruction provenance. This is historical SYN-005 verified still present in current source.
remediation: Pin base/toolchain and verify direct downloads; retain resolved build input identities.
reproduction_status: current source callpath inspection; no executable download or cloud operation

title: Raw-host remote validation still installs unverified tool archives
trigger: Run raw-host remote validation with a missing tool so prebuilt fallback paths are reached
impact: Latest release URL or mutable S3/tarball bytes are extracted and installed without independent checksum/signature/version identity. Version output does not establish approved bytes. Containerized routes may avoid this branch; no live exploitation or cloud execution was attempted.
remediation: Require exact approved version, digest and S3 VersionId where used; verify before extraction/execution.
reproduction_status: current source callpath inspection; no executable download or cloud operation

title: Dependency scaffold fills its bounded map with lifecycle locks
trigger: Generate dependency scaffold from the frozen complete repository packet
impact: The generated map contains80 lifecycle lock paths and no Cargo manifest/lock. Trusting this as coverage would omit actual dependencies. The current review replaced it with explicit manifest/lock inventory; generic tooling defect remains.
remediation: Use ecosystem-aware dependency classifiers, explicit lane assignments and reject empty material dependency denominators.
